micro_units.title: Task Routing
micro_units.core_question: Identify the mental or social variable that the question is really asking for
micro_units.decision_variable: the psychological or social variable required by the question
use_when: Use when you need to identify the mental or social variable that the question is really asking for.
Use when the answer depends on the psychological or social variable required by the question.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not solve the substantive problem; it only selects the capability entry point.

micro_units.title: Evidence-Chain Construction
micro_units.core_question: Separate textual evidence, inference, and commonsense completion
micro_units.decision_variable: which evidence supports the conclusion
use_when: Use when you need to separate textual evidence, inference, and commonsense completion.
Use when the answer depends on which evidence supports the conclusion.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not compare competing explanations; it organizes evidence sources.

micro_units.title: Multiple-Explanation Competition
micro_units.core_question: Preserve and compare several plausible interpretations
micro_units.decision_variable: which explanation best accounts for the available evidence
use_when: Use when you need to preserve and compare several plausible interpretations.
Use when the answer depends on which explanation best accounts for the available evidence.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not make a value judgment; it selects among explanations.

micro_units.title: Anti-Bias Check
micro_units.core_question: Prevent perspective bias, outcome bias, and moral-intuition shortcuts
micro_units.decision_variable: whether the current reasoning is being distorted by the solver's perspective or intuitive reaction
use_when: Use when you need to prevent perspective bias, outcome bias, and moral-intuition shortcuts.
Use when the answer depends on whether the current reasoning is being distorted by the solver's perspective or intuitive reaction.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not generate new explanations; it checks existing ones.

micro_units.title: Sensory Access
micro_units.core_question: Determine who can see, hear, touch, smell, or otherwise perceptually access what
micro_units.decision_variable: whether the character can contact the information through a sensory channel
use_when: Use when you need to determine who can see, hear, touch, smell, or otherwise perceptually access what.
Use when the answer depends on whether the character can contact the information through a sensory channel.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not judge whether the character noticed it; only whether it was perceptually available.

micro_units.title: Spatial Perspective Transformation
micro_units.core_question: Determine what is visible from another person's position
micro_units.decision_variable: the spatial relation visible from the target perspective
use_when: Use when you need to determine what is visible from another person's position.
Use when the answer depends on the spatial relation visible from the target perspective.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not judge belief; only viewpoint visibility.

micro_units.title: Attention and Salience
micro_units.core_question: Determine who noticed a key cue and who ignored it
micro_units.decision_variable: whether the information entered the character's attentional focus
use_when: Use when you need to determine who noticed a key cue and who ignored it.
Use when the answer depends on whether the information entered the character's attentional focus.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from sensory access; seeing is not the same as noticing.

micro_units.title: Temporal Order and Event Updating
micro_units.core_question: Determine how event order changes mental states
micro_units.decision_variable: the sequence of events and its updating effect
use_when: Use when you need to determine how event order changes mental states.
Use when the answer depends on the sequence of events and its updating effect.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not judge memory retention; only event order.

micro_units.title: Memory, Forgetting, and Misremembering
micro_units.core_question: Determine what a character knows, remembers, forgets, or misremembers
micro_units.decision_variable: the character's current memory state
use_when: Use when you need to determine what a character knows, remembers, forgets, or misremembers.
Use when the answer depends on the character's current memory state.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from knowledge boundary; this skill concerns retention or distortion after prior exposure.

micro_units.title: Knowledge Boundary
micro_units.core_question: Determine whether a character has the background knowledge needed to understand information
micro_units.decision_variable: whether the character has the required professional, cultural, experiential, or conceptual background
use_when: Use when you need to determine whether a character has the background knowledge needed to understand information.
Use when the answer depends on whether the character has the required professional, cultural, experiential, or conceptual background.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from perception and memory; it concerns background competence.

micro_units.title: First-Order Belief
micro_units.core_question: Determine what X believes the facts are
micro_units.decision_variable: the character's subjective representation of reality
use_when: Use when you need to determine what X believes the facts are.
Use when the answer depends on the character's subjective representation of reality.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the belief does not have to be false.

micro_units.title: False Belief
micro_units.core_question: Determine when X's belief conflicts with reality
micro_units.decision_variable: the discrepancy between belief and actual state
use_when: Use when you need to determine when X's belief conflicts with reality.
Use when the answer depends on the discrepancy between belief and actual state.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit requires a reality-belief conflict.

micro_units.title: Second-Order or Recursive Belief
micro_units.core_question: Determine what X thinks Y believes
micro_units.decision_variable: one mental model embedded inside another
use_when: Use when you need to determine what X thinks Y believes.
Use when the answer depends on one mental model embedded inside another.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from common knowledge; the focus is recursive attribution.

micro_units.title: Appearance-Reality Distinction
micro_units.core_question: Distinguish what something appears to be from what it actually is
micro_units.decision_variable: the gap between surface appearance and true state
use_when: Use when you need to distinguish what something appears to be from what it actually is.
Use when the answer depends on the gap between surface appearance and true state.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not require a specific character to hold a false belief.

micro_units.title: Evidence-Availability Updating
micro_units.core_question: Determine how newly available evidence changes belief
micro_units.decision_variable: the direction of belief update caused by new information
use_when: Use when you need to determine how newly available evidence changes belief.
Use when the answer depends on the direction of belief update caused by new information.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from source credibility; the focus is evidence availability and update effect.

micro_units.title: Common Knowledge
micro_units.core_question: Determine whether both parties know something and know that the other knows it
micro_units.decision_variable: whether knowledge is openly shared by both sides
use_when: Use when you need to determine whether both parties know something and know that the other knows it.
Use when the answer depends on whether knowledge is openly shared by both sides.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from second-order belief; the focus is public sharedness.

micro_units.title: Uncertain Belief
micro_units.core_question: Determine whether X is guessing, doubting, or only partially convinced
micro_units.decision_variable: the character's subjective certainty
use_when: Use when you need to determine whether X is guessing, doubting, or only partially convinced.
Use when the answer depends on the character's subjective certainty.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from source credibility; it concerns confidence level.

micro_units.title: Source Credibility
micro_units.core_question: Determine how rumors, eyewitness reports, authority, or deceptive sources affect belief
micro_units.decision_variable: the reliability of the information source
use_when: Use when you need to determine how rumors, eyewitness reports, authority, or deceptive sources affect belief.
Use when the answer depends on the reliability of the information source.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from uncertain belief; it concerns why confidence changes.

micro_units.title: Self Preference
micro_units.core_question: Determine what a character personally likes or wants
micro_units.decision_variable: the character's own preference
use_when: Use when you need to determine what a character personally likes or wants.
Use when the answer depends on the character's own preference.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not judge whether the character understands another person's preference.

micro_units.title: Other Preference
micro_units.core_question: Determine whether a character understands what someone else likes or wants
micro_units.decision_variable: the character's representation of another person's preference
use_when: Use when you need to determine whether a character understands what someone else likes or wants.
Use when the answer depends on the character's representation of another person's preference.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from self preference; it models another person's desire.

micro_units.title: Goal Hierarchy
micro_units.core_question: Distinguish long-term, short-term, and local goals
micro_units.decision_variable: the hierarchical relation among goals
use_when: Use when you need to distinguish long-term, short-term, and local goals.
Use when the answer depends on the hierarchical relation among goals.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not decide between conflicting goals.

micro_units.title: Intention Recognition
micro_units.core_question: Infer the purpose behind an action, gaze, gesture, or other cue
micro_units.decision_variable: the immediate purpose behind the behavior
use_when: Use when you need to infer the purpose behind an action, gaze, gesture, or other cue.
Use when the answer depends on the immediate purpose behind the behavior.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from action prediction; it explains why the current behavior occurs.

micro_units.title: Action Prediction
micro_units.core_question: Predict the next likely action from belief and goal
micro_units.decision_variable: what the character is most likely to do next
use_when: Use when you need to predict the next likely action from belief and goal.
Use when the answer depends on what the character is most likely to do next.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from intention recognition; it concerns future behavior.

micro_units.title: Commitment Priority
micro_units.core_question: Resolve priority among existing commitments, ongoing tasks, and new invitations
micro_units.decision_variable: the priority order among commitments or plans
use_when: Use when you need to resolve priority among existing commitments, ongoing tasks, and new invitations.
Use when the answer depends on the priority order among commitments or plans.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from general goal conflict; it requires a commitment or plan constraint.

micro_units.title: Goal-Conflict Arbitration
micro_units.core_question: Determine how a character chooses among conflicting goals
micro_units.decision_variable: the weighting rule for competing goals
use_when: Use when you need to determine how a character chooses among conflicting goals.
Use when the answer depends on the weighting rule for competing goals.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not require prior commitments; it applies to general goal competition.

micro_units.title: Basic Emotion Appraisal
micro_units.core_question: Infer emotion from success, failure, threat, loss, or gain
micro_units.decision_variable: how an event affects the character's goals or interests
use_when: Use when you need to infer emotion from success, failure, threat, loss, or gain.
Use when the answer depends on how an event affects the character's goals or interests.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not handle disguise, counterfactual emotion, or moral emotion.

micro_units.title: Atypical Emotion
micro_units.core_question: Explain why an unexpected or nonstandard emotion appears
micro_units.decision_variable: why the emotion deviates from ordinary expectation
use_when: Use when you need to explain why an unexpected or nonstandard emotion appears.
Use when the answer depends on why the emotion deviates from ordinary expectation.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when not the same as hidden emotion; the true feeling itself is unusual.

micro_units.title: Hidden Emotion
micro_units.core_question: Detect a mismatch between true feeling and outward display
micro_units.decision_variable: the difference between internal emotion and external expression
use_when: Use when you need to detect a mismatch between true feeling and outward display.
Use when the answer depends on the difference between internal emotion and external expression.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not explain the social rule behind hiding; only detects the mismatch.

micro_units.title: Emotional Disguise and Display Rules
micro_units.core_question: Explain why and how a character manages outward emotion for politeness, role, or situation
micro_units.decision_variable: the social rule governing emotional display
use_when: Use when you need to explain why and how a character manages outward emotion for politeness, role, or situation.
Use when the answer depends on the social rule governing emotional display.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from hidden emotion; the focus is rule-based expression control.

micro_units.title: Moral Emotion
micro_units.core_question: Infer guilt, shame, pride, anger, or gratitude from responsibility, norm, or value appraisal
micro_units.decision_variable: the responsibility or norm evaluation that triggers emotion
use_when: Use when you need to infer guilt, shame, pride, anger, or gratitude from responsibility, norm, or value appraisal.
Use when the answer depends on the responsibility or norm evaluation that triggers emotion.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from basic emotion; moral or normative appraisal must be present.

micro_units.title: Counterfactual Emotion
micro_units.core_question: Infer regret, relief, disappointment, or pleasant surprise from comparison with an alternative outcome
micro_units.decision_variable: the comparison between reality and a possible alternative
use_when: Use when you need to infer regret, relief, disappointment, or pleasant surprise from comparison with an alternative outcome.
Use when the answer depends on the comparison between reality and a possible alternative.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not handle simple success or failure emotion.

micro_units.title: Empathy and Emotional Contagion
micro_units.core_question: Determine how another person's emotion affects the self
micro_units.decision_variable: the transmission of another person's emotion into one's own state
use_when: Use when you need to determine how another person's emotion affects the self.
Use when the answer depends on the transmission of another person's emotion into one's own state.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from understanding another's emotion; the focus is being affected.

micro_units.title: Emotion Regulation
micro_units.core_question: Determine how a character suppresses, redirects, rationalizes, or comforts themselves
micro_units.decision_variable: how the character changes or manages their internal emotion
use_when: Use when you need to determine how a character suppresses, redirects, rationalizes, or comforts themselves.
Use when the answer depends on how the character changes or manages their internal emotion.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from display rules; it concerns internal regulation rather than external politeness.

micro_units.title: Literal Meaning
micro_units.core_question: Determine what an utterance explicitly says
micro_units.decision_variable: the sentence's explicit semantic content
use_when: Use when you need to determine what an utterance explicitly says.
Use when the answer depends on the sentence's explicit semantic content.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not infer hidden intention.

micro_units.title: Indirect Speech Act
micro_units.core_question: Determine the social action performed by an utterance, such as hinting, requesting, refusing, reminding, or warning
micro_units.decision_variable: what the utterance is doing socially
use_when: Use when you need to determine the social action performed by an utterance, such as hinting, requesting, refusing, reminding, or warning.
Use when the answer depends on what the utterance is doing socially.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from conversational implicature; it asks "what act is this sentence performing?".

micro_units.title: Conversational Implicature
micro_units.core_question: Infer what is communicated by context but not explicitly said
micro_units.decision_variable: the implicit information derived from context
use_when: Use when you need to infer what is communicated by context but not explicitly said.
Use when the answer depends on the implicit information derived from context.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from indirect speech act; it asks "what extra meaning was conveyed?".

micro_units.title: Truth, Lie, and Half-Truth
micro_units.core_question: Evaluate a statement's relation to the facts
micro_units.decision_variable: the truth status of the utterance content
use_when: Use when you need to evaluate a statement's relation to the facts.
Use when the answer depends on the truth status of the utterance content.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not judge whether the speaker intended to mislead.

micro_units.title: Misleading and Selective Expression
micro_units.core_question: Determine whether a true statement induces a false understanding
micro_units.decision_variable: whether the expression leads the listener toward an incorrect inference
use_when: Use when you need to determine whether a true statement induces a false understanding.
Use when the answer depends on whether the expression leads the listener toward an incorrect inference.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from lying; the stated content can be true.

micro_units.title: Speaker Motivation
micro_units.core_question: Infer why a speaker says something, such as politeness, face-saving, testing, avoidance, or ingratiation
micro_units.decision_variable: the speaker's motive for speaking that way
use_when: Use when you need to infer why a speaker says something, such as politeness, face-saving, testing, avoidance, or ingratiation.
Use when the answer depends on the speaker's motive for speaking that way.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from persuasion strategy; the goal need not be to change the listener's attitude.

micro_units.title: Audience Calibration
micro_units.core_question: Adapt expression to experts, novices, children, out-groups, or other listeners
micro_units.decision_variable: how the expression fits the listener's ability, identity, or stance
use_when: Use when you need to adapt expression to experts, novices, children, out-groups, or other listeners.
Use when the answer depends on how the expression fits the listener's ability, identity, or stance.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from persuasion; the focus is adaptation rather than influence.

micro_units.title: Persuasion Strategy
micro_units.core_question: Determine how to change another person's belief, attitude, or behavior
micro_units.decision_variable: the influence strategy directed at the listener
use_when: Use when you need to determine how to change another person's belief, attitude, or behavior.
Use when the answer depends on the influence strategy directed at the listener.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from negotiation; it is primarily one-way influence.

micro_units.title: Faux Pas and Offense
micro_units.core_question: Judge whether behavior or speech violates social appropriateness
micro_units.decision_variable: whether the act breaches social tact or creates embarrassment/offense
use_when: Use when you need to judge whether behavior or speech violates social appropriateness.
Use when the answer depends on whether the act breaches social tact or creates embarrassment/offense.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not assign responsibility or propose repair.

micro_units.title: Harm and Responsibility
micro_units.core_question: Determine who caused harm, whether it was intentional, and whether blame is appropriate
micro_units.decision_variable: responsibility for harm
use_when: Use when you need to determine who caused harm, whether it was intentional, and whether blame is appropriate.
Use when the answer depends on responsibility for harm.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from faux pas judgment; the focus is responsibility and blameworthiness.

micro_units.title: Fairness and Reciprocity
micro_units.core_question: Evaluate distribution, fairness, repayment, and taking advantage
micro_units.decision_variable: whether resources or obligations are fair and reciprocal
use_when: Use when you need to evaluate distribution, fairness, repayment, and taking advantage.
Use when the answer depends on whether resources or obligations are fair and reciprocal.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from negotiation; it evaluates norms rather than designing a deal.

micro_units.title: Trust and Reputation
micro_units.core_question: Evaluate reliability from past behavior and interpersonal history
micro_units.decision_variable: long-term reliability
use_when: Use when you need to evaluate reliability from past behavior and interpersonal history.
Use when the answer depends on long-term reliability.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from source credibility; it concerns interpersonal history rather than one information source.

micro_units.title: Power, Status, and Role
micro_units.core_question: Identify teacher/student, manager/subordinate, expert/novice, and related role structures
micro_units.decision_variable: the role structure between interaction partners
use_when: Use when you need to identify teacher/student, manager/subordinate, expert/novice, and related role structures.
Use when the answer depends on the role structure between interaction partners.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not choose a communication strategy; it identifies the structure.

micro_units.title: Group Identity
micro_units.core_question: Determine how in-group, out-group, stereotypes, or belonging shape interpretation and evaluation
micro_units.decision_variable: the effect of group membership
use_when: Use when you need to determine how in-group, out-group, stereotypes, or belonging shape interpretation and evaluation.
Use when the answer depends on the effect of group membership.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from power role; it concerns identity boundaries.

micro_units.title: Privacy, Secrets, and Boundaries
micro_units.core_question: Determine what information may be shared and what should remain private
micro_units.decision_variable: the boundary of information disclosure
use_when: Use when you need to determine what information may be shared and what should remain private.
Use when the answer depends on the boundary of information disclosure.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not handle repair after a boundary has already been crossed.

micro_units.title: Relationship Repair and Apology
micro_units.core_question: Identify when apology, explanation, compensation, or relationship easing is needed
micro_units.decision_variable: the repair need after relationship damage
use_when: Use when you need to identify when apology, explanation, compensation, or relationship easing is needed.
Use when the answer depends on the repair need after relationship damage.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from faux pas judgment; it concerns follow-up repair.

micro_units.title: Self-Presentation and Impression Management
micro_units.core_question: Manage self-information, image, disclosure order, and self-description
micro_units.decision_variable: the desired impression others should form
use_when: Use when you need to manage self-information, image, disclosure order, and self-description.
Use when the answer depends on the desired impression others should form.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from emotional display rules; it concerns overall image management.

micro_units.title: Negotiation, Concession, and Joint Plan
micro_units.core_question: Find compromise, trades, and mutually acceptable plans under disagreement
micro_units.decision_variable: how both sides adjust to form a joint solution
use_when: Use when you need to find compromise, trades, and mutually acceptable plans under disagreement.
Use when the answer depends on how both sides adjust to form a joint solution.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from persuasion; negotiation requires bilateral adjustment.

micro_units.title: Power Navigation and Hierarchical Communication
micro_units.core_question: Choose communication actions across hierarchy, including escalation, authorization, compliance, challenge, and retreat
micro_units.decision_variable: what communication move fits a power gap
use_when: Use when you need to choose communication actions across hierarchy, including escalation, authorization, compliance, challenge, and retreat.
Use when the answer depends on what communication move fits a power gap.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from role recognition; it concerns strategy under hierarchy.

micro_units.title: Vague Quantity Prior
micro_units.core_question: Interpret vague quantifiers such as some, most, almost none, or about half
micro_units.decision_variable: the approximate range implied by a vague quantifier
use_when: Use when you need to interpret vague quantifiers such as some, most, almost none, or about half.
Use when the answer depends on the approximate range implied by a vague quantifier.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit does not update after observation.

micro_units.title: Quantity Update After Partial Observation
micro_units.core_question: Revise an estimate after seeing a sample
micro_units.decision_variable: how sample evidence changes quantity estimates
use_when: Use when you need to revise an estimate after seeing a sample.
Use when the answer depends on how sample evidence changes quantity estimates.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from base rate; it focuses on sample-based updating.

micro_units.title: Base Rate and Typicality
micro_units.core_question: Judge likelihood from commonness or typicality
micro_units.decision_variable: background probability or category typicality
use_when: Use when you need to judge likelihood from commonness or typicality.
Use when the answer depends on background probability or category typicality.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from vague quantity; it concerns category likelihood.

micro_units.title: Causal Attribution
micro_units.core_question: Identify which person, event, or condition caused an outcome
micro_units.decision_variable: the cause of the result
use_when: Use when you need to identify which person, event, or condition caused an outcome.
Use when the answer depends on the cause of the result.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when this unit differs from responsibility judgment; causation need not include blame.

macro_units.title: Classic False-Belief Judgment
macro_units.core_question: where or how a character will act based on a false belief
macro_units.decision_variable: where or how a character will act based on a false belief
macro_units.direct_route_rule: Route immediately when the case is a first-order search-location belief after an unseen move.
use_when: Use when the scene matches the classic false-belief judgment prototype.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the scene is better explained by a narrower micro capability than differs from second-order mind and appearance-reality cases; the core is action based on false belief.

macro_units.title: Second-Order Mind and Common Knowledge
macro_units.core_question: how one character understands another character's understanding
macro_units.decision_variable: how one character understands another character's understanding
macro_units.direct_route_rule: Route immediately when one mind models another mind or shared knowledge is central.
use_when: Use when the scene matches the second-order mind and common knowledge prototype.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the scene is better explained by a narrower micro capability than differs from first-order false belief; the core is nested mindreading or shared knowledge.

macro_units.title: Appearance-Reality and Knowledge Boundary
macro_units.core_question: how appearance, reality, and a character's knowledge boundary jointly determine the answer
macro_units.decision_variable: how appearance, reality, and a character's knowledge boundary jointly determine the answer
macro_units.direct_route_rule: Route immediately when appearance conflicts with reality or world knowledge is fenced off.
use_when: Use when the scene matches the appearance-reality and knowledge boundary prototype.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the scene is better explained by a narrower micro capability than differs from false-belief action prediction; the core is conflict among appearance, truth, and knowledge boundary.

macro_units.title: Social Cues and Nonverbal Intention
macro_units.core_question: what intention or social action a nonverbal cue conveys
macro_units.decision_variable: what intention or social action a nonverbal cue conveys
macro_units.direct_route_rule: Route immediately when the cue is nonverbal and social inference or sender intention is asked.
use_when: Use when the scene matches the social cues and nonverbal intention prototype.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the scene is better explained by a narrower micro capability than differs from linguistic pragmatics; the core is intention explanation from nonverbal cues.

macro_units.title: Hidden Emotion and Atypical Emotion
macro_units.core_question: why a character's true feeling differs from outward display or ordinary expectation
macro_units.decision_variable: why a character's true feeling differs from outward display or ordinary expectation
macro_units.direct_route_rule: Route immediately when emotion must be inferred through suppression, reversal, or unusual appraisal.
use_when: Use when the scene matches the hidden emotion and atypical emotion prototype.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the scene is better explained by a narrower micro capability than differs from moral emotion; the core is a mismatch between real emotion and display or expectation.

macro_units.title: Moral Emotion and Responsibility Judgment
macro_units.core_question: what emotion or judgment follows from responsibility, harm, and norm evaluation
macro_units.decision_variable: what emotion or judgment follows from responsibility, harm, and norm evaluation
macro_units.direct_route_rule: Route immediately when guilt, shame, blame, or responsibility drives the emotion.
use_when: Use when the scene matches the moral emotion and responsibility judgment prototype.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the scene is better explained by a narrower micro capability than differs from general emotion appraisal; the core is responsibility, harm, and normative evaluation.

macro_units.title: Indirect Language and Conversational Meaning
macro_units.core_question: what the speaker really wants the listener to understand
macro_units.decision_variable: what the speaker really wants the listener to understand
macro_units.direct_route_rule: Route immediately when spoken words mean a request, warning, complaint, refusal, reminder, or invitation beyond literal text.
use_when: Use when the scene matches the indirect language and conversational meaning prototype.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the scene is better explained by a narrower micro capability than differs from lies and misleading language; the core is indirect expression and implicature.

macro_units.title: Lies, Half-Truths, and Misdirection
macro_units.core_question: how an utterance operates across truth value, motive, and misleading effect
macro_units.decision_variable: how an utterance operates across truth value, motive, and misleading effect
macro_units.direct_route_rule: Route immediately when truth status or wording motive under partial disclosure is central.
use_when: Use when the scene matches the lies, half-truths, and misdirection prototype.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the scene is better explained by a narrower micro capability than differs from ordinary indirect expression; the core is truth status, selective wording, and misleading effect.

macro_units.title: Persuasion, Advice, and Audience Calibration
macro_units.core_question: how to adapt expression to a listener and change their belief, attitude, or behavior
